column1: # Real Preeti samples for aksharkit.
# What goes here: text that was really typed in the Preeti font (copied from a
# real document, not made by a converter), with the correct Unicode beside it.
# One sample per line, three columns separated by a TAB:
#   preeti<TAB>unicode<TAB>where it came from
# - preeti: the raw characters as stored, exactly as they look with a normal
#   font (for example g]kfn). Do not retype them from the Unicode side.
# - unicode: the same words in correct Unicode Devanagari (for example नेपाल),
#   typed or checked by someone who reads Nepali.
# - where it came from: a few words, e.g. "my 2019 college notice, line 3".
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. Every line here becomes a
# test: aksharkit must turn column 1 into column 2 exactly. A failing line is
# useful: it shows a key or an ordering rule the converter has wrong. A sample
# cannot start with # (the Preeti key for ३): start it one word later.
# The lines below were added in 0.9.0 (24 November 2026). Each is a short
# excerpt from a public PDF that embeds a font named Preeti. Column 1 is the
# text of the Preeti font as stored in the PDF (pdftohtml -xml, that font
# only; runs of spaces from the PDF layout are written as one space). Column 2
# is what the page visibly prints: the page image and the converted text set
# in Noto Sans Devanagari were compared by eye, line by line. The comparison
# was made by the build assistant, not by a native reader of Nepali, so a
# reader's corrections are still welcome. Spellings are the document's own
# (शक्तीको, दक्षतापुर्वक), and one line keeps a typist's doubled sign (sf]]),
# which prints as a single one.
